question: There is a list of seven numbers. The average of the first four numbers is \(5,\) and the average of the last four numbers is \(8.\) If the average of all seven numbers is \(6\frac{4}{7},\) then the number common to both sets of four numbers is
solution:
An average gives a sum when multiplied by the number of entries. Thus the first four numbers have sum \(4\cdot5=20\), and the last four have sum \(4\cdot8=32\). The sum of all seven numbers is
\[
7\left(6+\frac47\right)=42+4=46.
\]
Adding the two four-number sums counts the fourth entry twice and every other entry once. Therefore the extra amount above the seven-number sum is exactly the common number:
\[
20+32-46=6.
\]
The common number is \(\boxed{6}\), choice B.
